coefficients: Flat AI-FinOps FTE added to the run team once the agentic run is active.
Human Readiness Index ramp floor — the minimum achievable adoption ramp regardless of how low readiness scores.
Human Readiness Index ramp slope — how much a readiness-score point moves the achievable ramp.
Realisation cap × on the productivity-uplift curve — how far towards the theoretical ceiling adoption can actually move Y3 velocity/lead-time.
Reference uplift factor feeding the same realisation curve as the cap above.
Agent capacity (indicative) factor over vFTE — the surplus throughput an agent can produce beyond the effort it replaces. Deliberately isolated from vFTE and cost.
Ceiling on how many Decision-Intelligence points the quality premium can cost, regardless of how large the premium itself gets.
How strongly the quality premium converts into the DI-bar penalty (before the cap above applies).
Cap on the AI-code quality-premium multiplier that feeds the verification tax and the DI-bar penalty.
Transitional setup headcount (lead + architect + coach) shown on Team-out — display only, its € is already inside the Setup total.
Cap on the supervision-share used when sizing the AgentOps run team from agent vFTE.
How strongly agent vFTE converts into supervision-share headcount, before the cap above applies.
Hard cap on the verification-tax multiplier — how much extra review cost AI-authored work can add, at most.
namespaces: The master on/off switch for every optional model-engine phase. Cross-cutting — each phase turns its own flag on via its own Enable button; there is no single home tab.
P1 · Loop convergence — review-cycle count/cost, calibrated per artefact class.
P2 · Verification tax — the review overhead AI-authored work adds, by class.
P3 · Supervision — Provisioned vs Constrained supervisor capacity, and the ramp/ceiling that mode applies to agent vFTE.
P4 · Monte Carlo — the stochastic layer's draw count, correlation and distributions.

P4-adjacent · Counterfactual baseline drift — secular productivity improvement the case would have seen anyway, subtracted from gross savings. A secondary control inside the P4 page, not its own phase.
The headline case NPV discount rate — the sponsor's WACC/hurdle rate. Distinct from FLOW.discountRate below (a different cash-flow, time-to-market NPV).
P5 · Flow & value — work-in-progress, cycle time and the time-to-market NPV this phase prices, kept isolated from the headline savings NPV.

Client-measured DORA values placed beside each derived read-out (deployment frequency, change-failure rate, lead time). Pulled forward into the P3 page rather than P5, since it consumes P1/P3 state only.
P6 · Evidence ledger — tier/source/as-of/owner per model driver, plus the case's current benchmarking stage (qualification / investment approval / gate review).
